A.explanation: Density $8 \times 10^2 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$ is less than water at about $1000 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$, so the stone would float rather than sink.

B.explanation: Density $2 \times 10^3 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$ is greater than water and has correct density units, so sinking is expected.

C.explanation: Unit $\text{N m}^{-3}$ is weight per unit volume, not mass density, so it cannot be a value of density.

D.explanation: Unit $\text{N m}^{-3}$ is incorrect for density, which must be in $\text{kg m}^{-3}$.

hints: Notice the stone sinks in water, so compare its density with the density of water at about $1000 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$.
Recall density is mass per unit volume with unit $\text{kg m}^{-3}$, while $\text{N m}^{-3}$ is force per unit volume.
Check which value is both larger than $1000 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$ and given in the correct density unit.
walkthrough: Recall the density of water is about $1000 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$ or $1.0 \times 10^3 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$.
For sinking, the average density of the stone must be greater than the density of water, so $\rho_{stone} > 1000 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$.
Check units: density $\rho = m/V$ has unit $\text{kg m}^{-3}$, not $\text{N m}^{-3}$ which includes weight as a force.
Option A is $800 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$, which is less dense than water and would float.
Only $2 \times 10^3 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$ is both denser than water and in correct units. This is option B.
